text: A point source of $100\mathrm{W}$ emits light with $5%$ efficiency. At a distance of $5\mathrm{m}$ from the source, the intensity produced by the electric field component is:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A point source of $100\mathrm{W}$ emits light with $5%$ efficiency. At a distance of $5\mathrm{m}$ from the source, the intensity produced by the electric field component is evaluated as follows:


[IMG]


The intensity at a distance of $5$ meters can be calculated as:

Intensity at 5 m $=\frac{5}{4π\times 5^{2}}\left (\frac{W}{m^{2}}\right )$

$=\frac{1}{20π}\left (\frac{W}{m^{2}}\right )$

Since the intensity due to the electric field component is half of the total intensity:

Intensity due to electric field $=\frac{1}{40π}\left (\frac{W}{m^{2}}\right )$

Thus, we arrive at our result:

$=\frac{1}{40π}\left (\frac{W}{m^{2}}\right )$

text:
A current carrying rectangular loop PQRS is made of uniform wire. The length $PR=QS=5\mathrm{cm}$ and $PQ=RS=100\mathrm{cm}$. If ammeter current reading changes from I to $2I$, the ratio of magnetic forces per unit length on the wire $PQ$ due to wire $RS$ in the two cases respectively $\left (f_{PQ}^{I}:f_{PQ}^{2I}\right )$ is:


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Force between two current carrying wire

$=\frac{μ_{0}I_{1}I_{2}}{2πd}\times L$

Here, $I_{1}$ & $I_{2}$ are equal

$F=\frac{μ_{0}I^{2}}{2πd}\times L$

$F\propto I^{2}$

$\frac{F_{I}}{F_{2I}}=\frac{I^{2}}{4I^{2}}=\frac{1}{4}$

text: A faulty thermometer reads $5^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$ in melting ice and $95^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$ in steam. The correct temperature on absolute scale will be $__________$ $\mathrm{K}$ when the faulty thermometer reads $41^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A thermometer scale is linear, so a reading divides the interval between the ice point and the steam point in the same ratio on every scale.

The faulty thermometer reads $5^{\circ }$ at the ice point and $95^{\circ }$ at the steam point, an interval of 90 divisions. For a reading of $41^{\circ }$:

$\dfrac{T_{C}-0}{100-0}=\dfrac{41-5}{95-5}=\dfrac{36}{90}=0.4\Rightarrow T_{C}=40^{\circ }\text{C}$

On the absolute scale, $T=40+273.15=313.15\text{K}\approx 313\text{K}$.

Hence, the answer is 313.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift

$\Rightarrow x=\frac{1}{2}$

So $n=2$

text: The velocity of a particle executing SHM varies with displacement $(x)$ as $4v^{2}=50-x^{2}$. The time period of oscillations is $\frac{x}{7}s$. The value of $x$ is $___________$. $(~$ Take $\left. π=\frac{22}{7}\right )$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$4v^{2}=50-x^{2}$

or $v=\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{50-x^{2}}$

Comparing the above equation with $v=ω\sqrt{A^{2}-x^{2}}$

$\Rightarrow ω=\frac{1}{2}$

& $A=\sqrt{50}$

so $\frac{2π}{T}=\frac{1}{2}$

$\Rightarrow T=4π\sec$

$=4\times \frac{22}{7}\sec$

$T=\frac{88}{7}\sec$

so $x=88$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift

text:
As shown in figure, a cuboid lies in a region with electric field $E=2x^{2}\hat{i}-4y\hat{j}+6\hat{k}\mathrm{N}/\mathrm{C}$. The magnitude of charge within the cuboid is $n\in _{0}C$.

The value of $n$ is $_________ ($if dimension of cuboid is $1\times 2\times 3\mathrm{m}^{3}$ )


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The cuboid occupies $0\leq x\leq 1$, $0\leq y\leq 2$, $0\leq z\leq 3$ (in m). The flux is found face by face, with outward normals.

Faces normal to $x$ (area $2\times 3=6\text{m}^{2}$): at $x=1$, $E_{x}=2(1)^{2}=2$, so the flux is $2\times 6=12$; at $x=0$, $E_{x}=0$, so the flux is $0$.

Faces normal to $y$ (area $1\times 3=3\text{m}^{2}$): at $y=2$, $E_{y}=-4(2)=-8$, so the flux is $-8\times 3=-24$; at $y=0$, $E_{y}=0$, so the flux is $0$.

Faces normal to $z$ (area $1\times 2=2\text{m}^{2}$): $E_{z}=6$ is the same on both faces, so the top face gives $+6\times 2=+12$ and the bottom face, with outward normal $-\hat{k}$, gives $-12$; together $0$.

$𝜙_{\text{net}}=12-24+0=-12\text{N m}^{2}\text{C}^{-1}$

By Gauss's law, $q_{\text{enc}}=ε_{0}𝜙_{\text{net}}=-12ε_{0}$, so the magnitude of the enclosed charge is $12ε_{0}$ C and $n=12$.

Hence, the answer is 12.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 30th January Evening Shift
